articleTitle: AC Drives: electrical disturbance problems and solutions
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Predicting and Assuring EMC in the Power Electronics Arena
abstract: This paper describes high-frequency electrical disturbances, i.e. emissions, produced by AC drives. Only voltage source inverters are considered. Potential problems and solutions are discussed. Historically, most industrial drives have been installed without radio interference suppression filters. However, interference suppression filters are sometimes required and the filtering solution used in a 12 amp, 3-phase drive is described. The drive is the smallest frame size in a range that extends to over 1000 amps.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EMC analysis for power electronic equipment
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Predicting and Assuring EMC in the Power Electronics Arena
abstract: Power electronic equipment, by the very nature of its operation and geometry, generates a very complex electromagnetic environment. Secondary electronic systems, used for drives, control and monitoring, have successfully operated in this environment for many years. With the introduction of the European (EC) Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) Directive, manufacturers now have to show that their products comply with the Directive. This means that not only must the equipment or system function in its self generated noise but it must also have an adequate level of electromagnetic immunity and allow unhindered use of other electrical apparatus. This paper outlines one approach to the design for electromagnetic compatibility of power electronic equipment and describes progress towards the production of an EMC design and analysis facility for complex environments.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A survey of some EM simulation packages suitable for EMC
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Predicting and Assuring EMC in the Power Electronics Arena
abstract: A selection of solver packages has been analysed to discover the range of software available for EMC simulation and design. The range of software embraces finite elements, the transmission line matrix method, various methods of moments and a very simple spread-sheet type approach. Some comparative analysis is presented but the main thrust is to indicate the role which the individual packages might play in industrial design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: General principles of EMC characterisation and interference suppression
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Predicting and Assuring EMC in the Power Electronics Arena
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) is the ability of equipment to withstand a certain amount of electromagnetic interference without contributing themselves excessive amounts of electromagnetic energy into the environment. EMC thus involves issues of susceptibility and emission, covers a very wide frequency spectrum, and must be designed into virtually all types of equipment incorporating any kind of electrical supply. Addresses topics in EMC of interest to the power electronics designer with emphasis on basic principles. The author discusses conducted and radiated interference, bandwidth, pulsed and high frequency signals, shielding, filtering and grounding and EMC as part of an optimised design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Do we need EMC product standards?
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Predicting and Assuring EMC in the Power Electronics Arena
abstract: The author discusses the historical and legal aspects of the European EMC Directive and the general technical aspect. The example of a power drive system is used to illustrate implementation of the Directive.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
